requirements_summary: Product team: mid-market SaaS powering personalized recommendations and conversational merchandising for B2B retailers. Primary workloads: embeddings for product similarity, reranking of search results, and low-latency personalization chat. Latency targets: p95 chat < 200ms, p99 < 400ms; reranking p95 < 150ms. Throughput: steady-state 150-300 qps mixed; spike handling to 800 qps. Cost sensitivity: minimize per-1k-token cost, interested in batching and quantization. Model preference: open or quantized variants (13B-70B tradeoffs); want automated routing to cheaper variant on non-critical calls. Routing/fallback: model-variant fallback + region failover (us-west-2 primary, us-east-1 secondary). Security: SSO (SAML), SOC2 evidence required, KMS for encryption-at-rest, audit logs, data residency limited to NA. Retention: 90 days by default with options for stricter retention for PII queries.
poc_plan: Phase 0 - Provision: dedicated GPU pool in us-west-2 (reserved baseline + burst), network peering and KMS integration; baseline monitoring dashboards pre-populated.

Phase 1 - Canary (week 1): 10% of production traffic routed to Dedicated pool (user-segmented - non-paying testers + internal), metrics collected: latency distribution, error rate, relevance score on synthetic prompts.
Phase 2 - Ramp (week 2-3): 10% -> 50% after health gates. Health gates: p95 latency regression < 10% vs hosted baseline, error rate < 0.5%, relevance delta < 3% on eval set.

Phase 3 - Failover & rollback drills (week 3): execute region failover (us-west-2 -> us-east-1) and simulate node failure; verify automatic fallback to smaller quantized variant if latency or cost thresholds breached.
Rollback policy: immediate rollback to hosted API if any of (1) p99 latency increases > 2x, (2) relevance regression > 4%, (3) error rate > 1% sustained 5m.
Model variants tested: ch-core-13b-q4 (default), ch-core-7b-q4 for fallback, experimental 30B quantized for high-quality queries; routing rules by endpoint (chat vs rerank).
Observability: Redwood Console dashboards, token-level cost breakdown, trace sampling on canary users, daily quality regressions report vs golden prompts.
Success criteria: meet p95/p99 latency targets, relevance regression <= 3% on eval prompts, predictable cost below $X per 1k tokens (detailed pricing in drive deck).

crm_notes: Summary: Cardinal Harvest is a mid-market product personalization SaaS evaluating Redwood after a hosted API pilot. They saw good quality on hosted but cost & isolation concerns pushed them toward Dedicated. They want a tight POC that proves cost/perf improvements without quality regressions. Key asks: VPC/KMS, canary traffic by user cohort, model-variant fallback, region failover, clear rollback rules, and an SOW that explains reserved vs burst economics. Internal politics: product wants speed, security wants isolation, finance will decide based on 12-month ARR impact. AE notes: prioritize fast SOW and an executable canary playbook; SE notes: instrument evals and golden prompts up-front. Blockers: legal SLA wording and egress pricing clarity.
